articles.title: Constitutional Gating and Deterministic Recovery for Multi-Agent LLM Negotiation: Ablations Against a Stateful Adversarial Gatekeeper
articles.summary: The paper tests a control stack for multi-agent LLM negotiation designed to reduce wasted model calls from loops, malformed outputs, and compliance deadlocks. In a controlled adversarial testbed, deterministic recovery via context purge and a canonical recovery message escaped deadlocks 5 of 5 times, while LLM-only steering escaped 0 of 5 times; however, broader call and token reduction hypotheses were not supported.
articles.advisor_relevance: This is early technical research rather than a commercial deployment, but it highlights a key enterprise AI adoption issue: agentic systems need deterministic controls, audit trails, and bounded cost structures before they can be trusted in production workflows. The findings support the broader investment theme that governance, orchestration, and reliability layers may become important complements to foundation models.

articles.title: Can LLMs Fix It Without Code? Toward Automated Verification of No-Code Bug Fixes
articles.summary: The paper evaluates an execution-based pipeline for verifying whether LLM-generated no-code bug fixes actually resolve reported software issues in a real browser environment.
